s:
Assertion (A): Nameri became a National Park in 1998.
Reason (R): CA|TS was launched at the 1st Asian Parks Congress in Japan in 2013.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Nameri became a National Park in 1998 and CA|TS was launched in Japan in 2013; both are true, but the 2013 launch of CA|TS cannot explain a 1998 event.

s: Nameri Tiger Reserve, associated with the Jia Bhoroli river, is located in which district of Assam?
x: Nameri Tiger Reserve is in Sonitpur, Assam.

s: Which group lists the CA|TS-accredited tiger reserves of Assam?
o: Satpura, Pench, Kanha, Panna and Bandhavgarh
x: The Assam entries in the 24-reserve CA|TS list are Manas, Kaziranga, Orang and Nameri; the other groups belong to other States.

s: Which group lists the CA|TS-accredited tiger reserves of Madhya Pradesh?
o: Satpura, Pench, Kanha, Panna and Bandhavgarh
x: Madhya Pradesh's CA|TS-accredited reserves are Satpura, Pench, Kanha, Panna and Bandhavgarh; the other groups are Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Assam.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CA|TS-accredited tiger reserves of Maharashtra?
o: Navegaon–Nagzira is in Madhya Pradesh's list, not Maharashtra's
x: Navegaon–Nagzira is listed among Maharashtra's CA|TS-accredited reserves, not Madhya Pradesh's; Pench, Melghat and Tadoba–Andhari are also in Maharashtra's list.

s: In which year was the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) established?
x: The National Tiger Conservation Authority was established in 2006. The other years refer to Project Tiger’s launch, Nameri’s National Park status, and the All India Tiger Estimation respectively.

s: According to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022, what was India's estimated tiger population?
x: The 2022 estimation put India's tiger population at 3,682; 3,167 was the camera-trapped minimum estimate.

s: How many tiger reserves in India are now CA|TS-accredited?
x: India now has 24 CA|TS-accredited tiger reserves, not 15; Assam has 4.

s: How many pillars and elements does the CA|TS framework, launched in 2013, have?
x: CA|TS has 7 pillars and 17 elements: the first 5 pillars are CA and the last 2 TS.

s: In which year was Project Tiger launched?
x: Project Tiger began on 1 April 1973 with 9 reserves.

s: Which State had the highest tiger population in the All India Tiger Estimation 2022?
x: Madhya Pradesh had 785 tigers, ahead of Karnataka (563) and Uttarakhand (560).

s: On which date is Global Tiger Day observed?
x: Global Tiger Day is 29 July.

s: Which tiger reserves of Assam are UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
x: Kaziranga and Manas are UNESCO sites; Manas was inscribed in 1985.

s: What is the IUCN status of the tiger?
x: The tiger is classified as Endangered, not Vulnerable.

s: During which observance was India's first high-altitude Snow Leopard Safari launched at Leh on 7 October 2026?
x: The safari was launched at Leh, Ladakh, on 7 October 2026 during Wildlife Week; International Snow Leopard Day falls on 23 October.

s: Which captive-bred birds were released at Sam in the Desert National Park near Jaisalmer?
x: Two captive-bred male Great Indian Bustards (Ardeotis nigriceps, Critically Endangered) were released at Sam in the Desert National Park.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SHAN Society and Ladakh Forest Department – Implementing bodies of the Snow Leopard Safari
Panthera uncia – Scientific name of the snow leopard
Ladakh's snow leopard population under SPAI 2024 – 477
Launch of the Snow Leopard Safari – International Snow Leopard Day
x: The safari was launched on 7 October 2026 during Wildlife Week, not on International Snow Leopard Day (23 October); the other pairs are correct.

s: How much annual rainfall does the Desert National Park in the Thar Desert receive?
x: The park covers over 3,160 sq km of the Thar and receives under 100 mm of rain.

s: By what share did stubble burning in Punjab fall in 2025 compared with 2021?
x: Stubble burning fell by 93% in Punjab and 91% in Haryana.

s: On which date was Haryana, with Chandigarh as its capital, formed?
x: Haryana was formed on 1 November 1966, and its capital is Chandigarh.

s: What is the IUCN status of the snow leopard?
x: The snow leopard is IUCN Vulnerable; the Great Indian Bustard is Critically Endangered.

s: According to SPAI 2024, India has about how many snow leopards?
x: SPAI 2024 counted 718 snow leopards in India, with Ladakh highest at 477.

s: What does Haryana's Parali Protection Force undertake before the paddy harvest?
o: Operation of city air-quality monitoring stations
Monitoring of PM2.5, PM10 and CO emissions
Field surveillance, drone monitoring and midnight patrols
x: Haryana's Parali Protection Force carries out field surveillance, drone monitoring and midnight patrols at district and block level before the paddy harvest to prevent stubble burning.

s: Under which Section of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 are Conservation Reserves declared?
x: Section 36A deals with Conservation Reserves; Section 6 with State Boards and 26A with sanctuaries.

s: The snow leopard is the State animal of which State?
x: The snow leopard is the State animal of Himachal Pradesh and the UT animal of Ladakh.

s: On which date is International Snow Leopard Day observed?
x: International Snow Leopard Day is on 23 October; Project Snow Leopard began in 2009.

s: In which year was Project Snow Leopard launched?
x: Project Snow Leopard began in 2009.

s: What is the IUCN status of the Great Indian Bustard?
x: The GIB (Ardeotis nigriceps) is Critically Endangered; its main threat is power lines.

s: The Great Indian Bustard is the State bird of which State?
x: The GIB is the State bird of Rajasthan.

s: Under which Section of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 are State Boards for Wildlife, chaired by the Chief Minister, set up?
x: Section 6 = State Boards (CM chairs); 36A = Conservation Reserves; 26A = final notification of sanctuaries.

s: What is the IUCN status of the Great Indian Bustard, the State bird of Rajasthan?
x: The Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) is Critically Endangered; its main threat is power lines.

s: The new gecko Hemidactylus koyaorum was found in which location of Telangana?
x: Hemidactylus koyaorum, named after the Koya tribe, was found in Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary, Warangal; Nalgonda is linked with H. cairnicola.

s: Whom does Didymocarpus nautiyalii, a new plant from Shi-Yomi district of Arunachal Pradesh, honour?
x: It is named after Prof. Sunil Nautiyal, former Director of the G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment.

s: The new gecko Hemidactylus cairnicola was found in which district of Telangana?
x: Hemidactylus cairnicola was found in Nalgonda district; Warangal (Pakhal WLS) is linked with H. koyaorum.

s: In which year was the Zoological Survey of India, headquartered in Kolkata, established?
x: ZSI was established in 1916 with headquarters in Kolkata.

s: The newly discovered plant Didymocarpus nautiyalii belongs to which family?
x: Didymocarpus nautiyalii is a Gesneriaceae herb of about 8 cm with leathery leaves and blue-violet flowers, growing on moist rocks above 1,000 m.

s: In which year was the Botanical Survey of India established?
x: BSI dates from 1890 and ZSI from 1916; both are headquartered in Kolkata.

s: Ophiorrhiza shidiensis and Ophiorrhiza pemae, found in Arunachal Pradesh, belong to which family?
x: Ophiorrhiza is in Rubiaceae (coffee family); Osbeckia is Melastomataceae and Didymocarpus Gesneriaceae.

s: Ophiorrhiza shidiensis and Ophiorrhiza pemae, new plants from Arunachal Pradesh, were discovered by Madras Christian College and which institution?
x: The two Rubiaceae plants from Vijaynagar, Changlang were described by the Botanical Survey of India and Madras Christian College, Chennai.

s: Researchers of which university described Osbeckia assamensis, a new plant from Manas National Park?
x: Osbeckia assamensis was described by Namita Nath of Gauhati University and Barnali Das of Pragjyotish College.

s: The new gecko Hemidactylus koyaorum honours which community?
x: H. koyaorum from Pakhal WLS, Warangal, honours the Koya tribe.

s: In which year were the Western Ghats declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: The Western Ghats became a UNESCO site in 2012.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the eight pollutants used for the Air Quality Index mentioned in relation to NCAP?
x: The eight pollutants include PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and lead. Methane is not included in this list.

s: In the air-quality context, what does PM10 refer to?
x: PM10 means particles with a size of 10 micrometres or less. The other options use incorrect units or refer to a different size threshold.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 Swachh Vayu Survekshan awards?
o: The 5th awards were presented on 7 September 2026
Jammu Municipal Corporation was recognised in all three ward categories
Municipal wards were included for the first time in 2025
x: Municipal wards were included for the first time in 2026, not 2025; the other statements are correct.

s: Which city won the 10 lakh+ category of Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026?
x: Lucknow won the 10 lakh+ category in 2026 (Indore had won in 2025); Rourkela and Kalinganagar won the smaller categories.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026?
o: It was the fifth edition, announced on 7 September 2026.
Kalinga Nagar topped the under-3-lakh category.
Guntur topped the 3–10 lakh population category.
x: Rourkela topped the 3–10 lakh category; Guntur was joint 2nd.

s: In which year did the UNGA designate 7 September as the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies?
x: The UNGA designated the day in 2019; it was first observed in 2020.

s: Implementation of the National Clean Air Programme is tracked through which portal?
x: NCAP, covering 130 cities, is tracked through the PRANA portal.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Air Act dates to 1981; NAAQS is from 2009 (12 pollutants), the National AQI from 2015 and GRAP from 2017 for Delhi-NCR.

s: OCEMS (Online Continuous Emission Monitoring System) is mandated for how many categories of highly polluting industries?
x: OCEMS is mandated for 17 categories of highly polluting industries, not 71.

s: In which year was the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Act enacted?
x: The CAQM Act dates from 2021, not 2022.

s: Which app provides the Air Quality Index for 292+ Indian cities?
x: SAMEER gives AQI for 292+ cities; PRANA is the portal that tracks NCAP.

s: Where did PM Modi launch Mission LiFE on 20 October 2022?
x: Mission LiFE was launched by PM Modi at Kevadia, Gujarat, on 20 October 2022.

s: Which city won the 3-10 lakh population category of Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026?
x: Rourkela won Category-2 (3-10 lakh) with 198.5 marks; Guntur was joint second.

s: How many stages does the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) for Delhi-NCR have?
x: GRAP has 4 stages, from Poor (AQI 201-300) to Severe Plus (above 450).

s: Which city won the under-3-lakh population category of Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026?
x: Category-3 winner in 2026 was Kalinganagar (Dewas won in 2025).

s: In India's Air Quality Index, which range is classed as 'Severe'?
x: AQI Very Poor = 301-400; Severe = 401-500.

s: What is the target of the Nagar Van Yojana by 2026-27?
x: Nagar Van Yojana targets 1,000 urban forests by 2026-27; 626 have been supported.

s: Under the CPCB classification of industries, which category has the least polluting industries?
x: CPCB ranks industries from Red (most polluting) through Orange and Green to White, which is the least polluting (practically non-polluting). Blue is a separate category for essential environmental services.

s: Short-Lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs) are also known as which of the following?
x: SLCPs are also called super pollutants and Short-Lived Climate Forcers. Sulphate aerosols are cooling particles, not an alternative name for SLCPs.

s: The Global Methane Pledge, which India has not joined, calls for a methane cut of how much from 2020 levels by 2030?
x: The pledge calls for a 30% reduction from 2020 levels by 2030; India is not a member.

s: Which set lists India's measures against household and agricultural emission sources?
o: PMUY, GRAP, National AQI, SRI and Kigali Amendment
SRI, Global Methane Pledge, NAAQS, DSR and GRAP
GOBARdhan, Montreal Protocol, DSR, Air Act and PMUY
PMUY, GOBARdhan, SRI, DSR and alternate wetting & drying
x: The listed measures are PMUY, GOBARdhan, SRI, DSR and alternate wetting & drying; the other sets mix in air-quality rules or international instruments.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Global Methane Pledge – UNEP-led; India joined in 2019
Climate and Clean Air Coalition – Adopted in 2016
x: The Montreal Protocol dates to 1987. The Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016, the Global Methane Pledge came at COP26 Glasgow (2021), and the CCAC is UNEP-led with India joining in 2019.

s: Short-Lived Climate Pollutants cause up to what share of present warming?
x: SLCPs cause up to 45% of present warming.

s: Which of the following comprises the major warming Short-Lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs)?
o: Carbon dioxide, sulphate aerosols, water vapour and nitrogen
Sulphate aerosols, stratospheric ozone, nitrogen and oxygen
Black carbon, methane, tropospheric ozone and HFCs
Methane, sulphate aerosols, stratospheric ozone and VOCs
x: The major warming SLCPs are black carbon, methane, tropospheric ozone and HFCs. Sulphate aerosols cool, while tropospheric ozone is formed from precursor gases rather than being directly emitted.

s: Ozone causes the loss of approximately how much staple crops every year?
x: Ozone causes the loss of about 110 million tonnes of staple crops annually, not 100 million.

s:
Consider the following statements about Short-Lived Climate Pollutants:
1. Black carbon is a greenhouse gas.
2. Tropospheric ozone is not directly emitted.
3. Sulphate aerosols have a cooling effect.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct; black carbon is a particle that absorbs radiation, not a greenhouse gas.

s: Over 20 years, methane warms the planet about how many times more than CO2?
x: Methane has about 80 times the warming effect of CO2 over 20 years.

s: Why are the HFCs controlled under the Kigali Amendment regulated?
x: HFCs do not deplete ozone; the Kigali Amendment phases them down for their warming effect.

s: Which organisation leads the Climate and Clean Air Coalition, which India joined in 2019?
x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is UNEP-led; India joined in 2019.

s: Which sector accounts for the largest share of India's methane emissions?
x: As per India's Third Biennial Update Report (2016 data), agriculture gives about 74% of India's methane.

s: In which year was the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer adopted?
x: Vienna Convention 1985; Montreal Protocol 1987.

s: On which date is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer (Ozone Day) observed?
x: Ozone Day is 16 September, the date the Montreal Protocol was adopted in 1987.

s: Where was the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol adopted on 15 October 2016?
x: The Kigali Amendment (HFC phase-down) was adopted at Kigali, Rwanda.

s: Where is UNEP, which hosts the Ozone Secretariat, headquartered?
x: UNEP was set up in 1972 with HQ at Nairobi.

s: At which conference was the Global Methane Pledge launched?
x: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26 Glasgow (2021); India has not joined it.

s: Where is the secretariat of the UNFCCC located?
x: The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn; the CBD's is in Montreal and UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi.

s: On which date did the Paris Agreement, adopted at COP21 in 2015, enter into force?
x: The Paris Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016.

s: According to UNEP's 2026 Emissions Gap Report, the new NDCs cut emissions by only about how much by 2030?
x: New NDCs cut emissions only 5–8% by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035, far short of the 18% needed by 2030.

s: Tuvalu, threatened by sea-level rise, is which of the following?
x: Tuvalu, about 26 sq km, is the world's fourth-smallest country.

s: Which organisation released the Emissions Gap Report 2026 titled 'The Point of Return'?
x: The Emissions Gap Report is an annual UNEP report; its 17th edition in 2026 was titled 'The Point of Return'.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UNFCCC:
1. It was adopted at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1994.
3. Its secretariat is in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: UNFCCC was adopted in 1992 at Rio and came into force on 21 March 1994; its secretariat is in Bonn.

s: What is the currency of Tuvalu?
x: Tuvalu uses the Australian Dollar.

s: With which animal is Bhitarkanika, a Ramsar site in Odisha, associated?
x: Bhitarkanika is known for estuarine crocodiles; the Royal Bengal Tiger is associated with the Sundarbans.

s: What is Tso Kar, for which Ladakh launched a restoration initiative?
o: High-altitude saline lake-wetland complex in southeastern Ladakh
High-altitude freshwater lake in western Ladakh
Glacial lake in the Zanskar valley
Riverine wetland on the Indus near Leh
x: Tso Kar, also called the 'White Lake', is a high-altitude saline lake-wetland complex in southeastern Ladakh.

s: In which year was the Tso Kar Wetland Complex in Ladakh, a Black-necked Crane habitat, designated a Ramsar site?
x: The Tso Kar Wetland Complex, comprising Tso Kar and Startsapuk Tso, was designated a Ramsar site in 2020.

s: Where will COP18 of the Convention on Biological Diversity be held in 2028?
x: COP17 was at Yerevan in 2026; COP18 is set for Quito, Ecuador in 2028.

s: Which of the following has its secretariat in Montreal?
x: The CBD secretariat is in Montreal; IUCN, WWF and the Ramsar secretariat are at Gland.

s: Where was COP17 of the Convention on Biological Diversity held in October 2026?
x: CBD COP17 was held at Yerevan, Armenia (19-31 Oct 2026); it adopted the Yerevan Pathway.

s: Which were India's first Ramsar sites, designated in 1981?
o: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
x: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park were India's first Ramsar sites (1981).

s: Which State has the largest number of Ramsar sites in India?
x: Tamil Nadu has the most Ramsar sites in India.

s: At which CBD Conference of the Parties was the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework adopted?
x: KMGBF was adopted at COP15 Montreal (2022): 4 goals for 2050, 23 targets for 2030.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsar Convention:
1. It was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971.
2. India joined it in 1982.
3. Its secretariat is in Montreal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ramsar: adopted 2 Feb 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; India joined 1 Feb 1982; secretariat Gland, Switzerland.

s: On which date is World Wetlands Day observed?
x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February.

s: In which year was the IUCN established?
x: IUCN was set up in 1948, HQ Gland, Switzerland.

s: Where is the headquarters of the FAO, whose Committee on Forestry (COFO 28) met in 2026?
x: FAO (est. 16 Oct 1945) is headquartered in Rome.

s: What forest-cover target does India's National Forest Policy, 1988 set?
x: The National Forest Policy 1988 targets 33% forest cover; present forest and tree cover is 25.17%.

s: What additional carbon sink has India committed to create by 2030 under its NDC?
x: India's NDC: extra carbon sink of 2.5-3 billion tonnes CO2e by 2030.

s: Which report, titled 'The Science of Hope', found in October 2026 that monitored wildlife populations fell by an average of 73% between 1970 and 2022?
x: WWF and ZSL's Living Planet Report 2026 put the average fall at 73% (1970-2022).

s: According to the Living Planet Report 2026, which type of wildlife populations showed the steepest decline since 1970?
x: Freshwater populations fell most (85%), then terrestrial (69%) and marine (59%).

s: At which CBD COP was the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework adopted in 2022?
x: The KMGBF was adopted at CBD COP15, Montreal, in 2022; it has 4 goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030.

s: Where is the secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
x: The CBD, adopted at the 1992 Rio Summit and in force from 29 December 1993, has its secretariat in Montreal.

s: What forest-cover target does the National Forest Policy, 1988 set for India?
x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 targets one-third (33%) of the geographical area under forest cover.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s: Which of the following is the primary objective of the MISHTI scheme?
o: Increasing mangrove cover and conserving mangrove ecosystems
Regulating commercial activities in coastal zones

s: What is Samudrayaan under the Deep Ocean Mission (2021–2026)?
x: Samudrayaan is a manned deep-sea mission under the Deep Ocean Mission for 2021–2026.

s: The UN Ocean Decade covers which period?
x: The UN Ocean Decade runs from 2021 to 2030.

s: National Coastal Mission 2.0, with an outlay of ₹767 crore, covers which period?
x: NCM 2.0 is a Central Sector Scheme for 2025–26 to 2030–31 with ₹767 crore; 2021–22 to 2025–26 was the NCM 1.0 period.

s: How many coastal States and UTs does National Coastal Mission 2.0, directly administered by MoEFCC, cover?
x: NCM 2.0 covers 9 coastal States and 4 UTs and is directly administered by MoEFCC.

s: What area does Sewell Rise-01, an offshore block notified near Great Nicobar, cover?
x: Sewell Rise-01 covers 632 sq km; West Sewell Ridge-01 covers 1,000 sq km.

s: The Pichavaram Mangrove Forest, subject of an economic valuation and blue carbon study, is in which State?
x: The study 'Economic Valuation and Blue Carbon Assessment of Ecosystem Services in the Pichavaram Mangrove Forest' concerns Pichavaram in Tamil Nadu.

s: According to the Pichavaram mangrove study, where is most mangrove carbon stored?
x: The study (302 households in 5 villages) found mangrove carbon mostly stored below ground in sediments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about mangroves?
o: ISFR 2023 recorded India's mangrove cover at 4,992 sq km.
Mangroves are called the 'Lungs of the Planet'.
IUCN 2024 reported 50% of the world's mangrove ecosystems at risk of collapse.
x: Mangroves are called the 'Kidneys of the Planet', not the 'Lungs of the Planet'.

s: In which year was India's Deep Ocean Mission (outlay ₹4,077 crore) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences launched?
x: The Deep Ocean Mission was launched in 2021, not 2020.

s: Up to what distance does the Exclusive Economic Zone extend under UNCLOS?
x: The EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles under UNCLOS, not 12.

s: What is the outlay of MISHTI, the mangrove initiative launched in 2023?
x: MISHTI (2023) has ₹100 crore; ₹767 crore is National Coastal Mission 2.0.

s: Which State has the largest mangrove cover in India according to ISFR 2023?
x: ISFR 2023: mangrove cover is highest in West Bengal, then Gujarat and the A&N Islands.

s: In September 2025, India became the first country to hold two International Seabed Authority contracts for exploring which resource?
x: India became the first country with two ISA polymetallic sulphide contracts, executed by NCPOR, Goa.

s: Where is the Clarion-Clipperton Zone of polymetallic nodules located?
o: In the Central Indian Ocean Basin
Off Mexico in the Pacific Ocean
x: ISA nodule zones: Clarion-Clipperton (off Mexico), Central Indian Ocean Basin, Peru Basin.

s: Which institution executes India's International Seabed Authority contracts for polymetallic sulphides?
x: The ISA sulphide contracts are executed by NCPOR, Goa (est. 1998).

s: Which shipyard launched the research vessel Sagar Manthan for NCPOR?
x: Sagar Manthan was launched by GRSE (built at Rishi Bankim Shipyard, Kolkata) for NCPOR.

s: Which of the following are adaptations of mangroves?
x: Mangroves have pneumatophores (breathing roots), prop roots and vivipary (seeds germinate on the tree).

s: What is the length of India's coastline as per the latest estimate?
x: India's coastline is put at 11,098 km in the latest estimate, up from the older 7,516 km figure.

src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
s: Which of the following statements regarding Project Snow Leopard is INCORRECT?
o: Project Snow Leopard was launched in 2009.
For conservation, India has identified three large landscapes confined to Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh.
Nanda Devi - Gangotri, in Uttarakhand, is one such landscape.
The Convention on Migratory Species included the snow leopard as a Concerted Action Species under Appendix I.

s: Which among the following rare natural phenomenon is going to happen in 2024, after 221 (2) Glow Worm Caves 121. S years, in the United States of America?
x: The 2024 double cicada emergence (Brood XIII and Brood XIX together, first in 221 years) is the correct answer. The notes do not mention cicadas or this phenomenon, so no line supports it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Himalayan hazard-mitigation measures?
o: National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme – ₹150 crore; Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand
National Landslide Risk Mitigation Project – ₹1,000 crore; 15 States
CWC and NRSC-ISRO monitoring from 2025 covers 2,843 water bodies, including 2,485 glacial lakes
NDMA Guidelines on GLOFs were issued in 2021
x: The NDMA Guidelines on GLOFs were issued in 2020, not 2021; 2021 is the year of the Dam Safety Act. The GLOF programme (₹150 crore, four Himalayan States) and the landslide project (₹1,000 crore, 15 States) are correctly stated.

s: Which volcano erupted in the Philippines in October 2026, sending ash up to 6 km?
x: Mount Kanlaon erupted in the Philippines, with ash reaching up to 6 km. Mayon, Taal and Pinatubo are other volcanoes associated with the Philippines, but they are not the volcano identified in this eruption event.

s: The Anak Krakatau eruption of September 6, 2026 occurred in which waterway?
o: Java Sea, between Java and the Indian Ocean
Andaman Sea, between Great Nicobar and Sumatra
Sewell Rise, in the Central Indian Ocean Basin
Sunda Strait, between Java and Sumatra
x: Anak Krakatau erupted in the Sunda Strait, which lies between Java and Sumatra. The Sunda Strait links the Java Sea with the Indian Ocean; that description does not make the Java Sea itself the eruption site.

s: In 2026, Swiss glaciers lost what share of their remaining ice?
x: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their remaining ice in 2026, the second-highest loss after 2022.

s: Uttarakhand's first real-time, solar-powered GLOF early warning system at Vasundhara Lake is in which district?
x: The system is located at Vasundhara Lake in Chamoli district.

s: Where is Mount Kanlaon, an active stratovolcano whose ash reached up to 6 km, located?
x: Kanlaon is on Negros Island in the Visayas, Philippines.

s: What is the summer capital of Uttarakhand?
x: Gairsain is Uttarakhand's summer capital; Dehradun is the capital.

s: Which conditions were among the causes of the record melting of Aletsch Glacier in 2026?
o: Record summer heatwaves and high winter snowfall
Cool summers and high winter snowfall
Cool summers and low winter snowfall
Record summer heatwaves and low winter snowfall
x: Record summer heatwaves and low (not high) winter snowfall contributed to the melting.

s: Which Chinese port, upgraded at a cost of $175.8 million, was buried in the August 2026 disaster?
x: Gyirong Port in Tibet, upgraded at $175.8 million, was buried in the August 2026 disaster.

s: The Nepal flash flood near the Nepal–China border on August 26, 2026, was identified as which of the following?
x: The event was a rock–ice collapse-triggered debris flood, not a conventional GLOF. The initial 4.4-magnitude earthquake reading was revised after the USGS attributed the signal to the collapse.

s: Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatau') rose from the caldera of the Krakatau eruption of which year?
x: Anak Krakatau rose from the caldera of the 1883 Krakatau eruption.

s: After the Nepal rock–ice collapse of August 2026, which barrage did India keep under watch?
x: India watched the Valmikinagar Barrage, not Farakka, and alerted Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Flash floods in the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli rivers — Nepal
Oil spill off Qeshm Island — Sri Lanka
x: The flash floods affecting the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers occurred in Nepal. The Qeshm Island oil spill was in Iran, Cyclone Ditwah affected Sri Lanka, and the Bald Range wildfire occurred in Canada.

s: At what wind speed is a cyclone in the North Indian Ocean given a name?
x: A name is assigned at 34 knots (about 63 km/h), sequentially, not by the landfall country.

s: In which country did the Qeshm Island oil spill take place?
x: Qeshm Island, site of the oil spill, belongs to Iran.

s: Which country was hit by Cyclone Ditwah?
x: Cyclone Ditwah struck Sri Lanka.

s: Which centre names the tropical cyclones of the North Indian Ocean?
x: RSMC New Delhi (IMD) names North Indian Ocean cyclones from the WMO/ESCAP Panel list.

s: The Aletsch Glacier, the largest and longest glacier in the Alps, is in which country?
x: Aletsch is a valley glacier in Switzerland and part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO site.

s: Near which place was Cyclone Arnab expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on 28 October 2026?
x: Severe cyclonic storm Arnab was expected to cross the AP coast near Yanam.

s: How many member countries does the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones, which names North Indian Ocean cyclones, have?
x: The Panel has 13 members, each giving 13 names (list adopted April 2020).

s: What are tropical cyclones of the north-west Pacific called?
x: Hurricanes = North Atlantic and NE/central North Pacific; typhoons = NW Pacific; willy-willy = old Australian term.

s: Where is the World Meteorological Organization headquartered?
x: WMO (est. 1950) is headquartered at Geneva.

s: In which country did the Bald Range wildfire occur?
x: The Bald Range wildfire was in Canada.

s: The Siang river of Arunachal Pradesh is known in Tibet by which name?
x: Brahmaputra = Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibet) = Siang (Arunachal).

s: Tropical cyclones in the North-West Pacific are called by which name?
x: Tropical cyclones are called typhoons in the North-West Pacific and hurricanes in the North Atlantic; 'willy-willy' is an old Australian term.

s: By which name is the Brahmaputra known in Arunachal Pradesh?
x: The Brahmaputra is the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet and the Siang in Arunachal; it joins the Dibang and Lohit in Assam.

s: As per State Energy Efficiency Index , 2024 released by BEE ( Bureau of Energy Efficiency ) , which State stood as top performer ?
x: In BEE's State Energy Efficiency Index 2024 (released 29 Aug 2025), Maharashtra is listed first and ranked top, as the Group 1 (>15 MToE) topper; Andhra Pradesh topped only Group 2.

s: Which organisation, headquartered in New Delhi, functions under the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
x: The Central Water Commission was set up in 1945, has its headquarters in New Delhi and works under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Deltares is a Netherlands-based partner in the Kalpasar Project.

s: Under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016 framework, India is a party to which convention on hazardous wastes?
x: The Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016 are the relevant framework and India is a party to the Basel Convention.

s: On which date did the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 come into force?
x: The GI Act was enacted in 1999 and came into force on 15 September 2003.

s: Why did the UN General Assembly promote equal-area world maps in place of the Mercator projection?
x: The Mercator projection enlarges high latitudes, which prompted the push for equal-area maps.

s: Why is the Mercator projection useful for navigation?
o: It shows continents at their true area
It shows high latitudes at true size
Constant compass bearings appear as straight lines
It keeps area, shape and distance together
x: On the Mercator projection constant compass bearings are straight lines, which suits navigation.

s: India's first port-based e-methanol plant is associated with which port authority?
x: The plant is associated with Deendayal Port Authority at Gandhidham–Kandla, Gujarat; Mumbai Port Authority is linked with Jawahar Dweep.

s: Which facility was declared India's first plastic-free oil terminal during Swachhata Abhiyan–2026?
x: The Mumbai Port Authority declared Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal India's first plastic-free oil terminal during Swachhata Abhiyan–2026.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's first port-based e-methanol plant?
o: Its partners are Deendayal Port Authority and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd.
It will produce a green marine fuel.
Its capacity is 500 tonnes per day.
Its inputs are renewable electricity, water and biogenic CO2.
x: The plant's capacity is 150 tonnes per day, not 500.

s: Jarjatta village in Raidih block, the main production centre of the GI-tagged Mandar, is in which district of Jharkhand?
x: Jarjatta village in Raidih block is in Gumla district, not Ranchi.

s: The Kalpasar Project MoUs signed at the 9th India International Water Week involved which Netherlands-based partners?
o: Deltares and Delft University of Technology
Rijkswaterstaat and Delft University of Technology
x: The two tripartite MoUs involved the Central Water Commission, Gujarat's Kalpasar Department, Deltares and Delft University of Technology.

s: What is Mandar, the GI-tagged instrument of Jharkhand?
o: Double-sided drum of red clay and leather
x: Mandar is a double-sided barrel or cylindrical drum made of red clay and leather, linked to the tribal culture of the Chotanagpur Plateau.

s: Across which water body does the Kalpasar Project envisage a roughly 30-km dam?
x: Kalpasar proposes a dam across the Gulf of Khambhat, creating a freshwater reservoir mainly for Saurashtra.

s: Which product was the first Geographical Indication registered in India (2004–05)?
x: Darjeeling Tea was India's first GI, registered in 2004–05.

s: India is the world's what-largest generator of e-waste, after China and the USA?
x: India is the third-largest generator of e-waste after China and the USA. The first and second positions are therefore not India's rank.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's e-waste and battery-waste rules?
o: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 came into force on 1 April 2023
The EPR recycling target rises to 80% from 2027-28
E-Waste Rules cover 106 categories, including solar PV
Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 permit landfilling and incineration of waste batteries
x: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 ban landfilling and incineration of waste batteries; the other statements are correct.

s: Who released the State Energy Efficiency Index 2024?
x: The 6th State Energy Efficiency Index (2024) is by BEE.

s: Which State topped the State Energy Efficiency Index 2024?
x: Maharashtra topped; Andhra Pradesh, Assam and Tripura led their groups.

s: In which State is Mawmluh Cave, among the first 100 IUGS geological heritage sites, located?
x: Mawmluh Cave is in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya.

s: Which body has recognised Mawmluh Cave as a geological heritage site?
x: Mawmluh Cave is among the first 100 geological heritage sites of the IUGS.

s: Which country moved the UNGA resolution promoting equal-area world maps ('Correct the Map')?
x: Togo moved the resolution; 164 of 193 voted in favour, including India, while the USA voted against.

s: Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad, which got a GI tag in October 2026, belongs to which State?
x: Ambaji Mohanthal Prasad is the gram-flour sweet of Ambaji Temple, Banaskantha, Gujarat.

s: Besides Assam and Tripura, which State led its group in the State Energy Efficiency Index 2024?
x: In BEE's State Energy Efficiency Index 2024, Maharashtra topped and Andhra Pradesh, Assam and Tripura led their groups.

s: Where is India's Geographical Indications Registry located?
x: The GI Registry (CGPDTM, DPIIT) is at Chennai.

s: Which country voted against the UNGA resolution promoting equal-area world maps?
x: 164 of 193 voted in favour, including India; the USA voted against.

s: Mayon Volcano, which erupted on 1 November 2026, is in Albay on which island?
x: Mayon is in Albay on Luzon; Mount Kanlaon is on Negros Island.

s:
Arrange the following events of 2026 in chronological order:
1. Eruption of Mount Kanlaon, Philippines
2. M6.5 earthquake in the Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands, Japan
3. Eruption of Mayon Volcano, Philippines
x: Mount Kanlaon erupted on 16 October 2026, the Bonin Islands earthquake struck on 26 October 2026 and Mayon erupted on 1 November 2026.

s: Tuvalu, threatened by sea-level rise, has which city as its capital?
x: Funafuti is the capital of Tuvalu, a country of about 26 sq km.

s: Tuvalu, formerly known as the Ellice Islands, consists of how many islands?
x: Tuvalu has nine islands (four reef islands and five atolls); its currency is the Australian Dollar.

s: Which city of Turkiye will host COP31 from 9 to 20 November 2026?
x: COP31 will be held at the Expo Center, Antalya, Turkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026.

s: Which country leads the negotiations at COP31, hosted by Turkiye in November 2026?
x: Turkiye hosts COP31 (9–20 November 2026), but Australia leads the negotiations.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: CBD COP18 will be held in Quito, Ecuador, in 2028. CBD COP17 was in Yerevan, COP31 is in Antalya and Australia leads COP31 negotiations.

s: With the addition of Sukhna Wetland and Sauj Jheel on 20 October 2026, India's Ramsar sites rose to how many?
x: With Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh), India's Ramsar sites rose to 103.

s: In which State is Sauj Jheel, added as a Ramsar site in October 2026, located?
x: Sauj Jheel is in Uttar Pradesh, not Uttarakhand; Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) was added the same day.

s: Which State launched India's first state-level Red List Assessment of Ecosystems on 20 October 2026?
x: Kerala launched India's first state-level Red List Assessment of Ecosystems through the Kerala State Biodiversity Board.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kerala's Red List Assessment of Ecosystems launched in October 2026?
o: It is India's first state-level Red List Assessment of Ecosystems.
It is being carried out by the Kerala State Biodiversity Board (KSBB).
It will cover 12 districts of Kerala.
It is to be completed in one year.
x: The assessment covers all 14 districts of Kerala, not 12.

s: The Kigali Amendment, which completed 10 years in October 2026, entered into force on which date?
x: The Kigali Amendment was adopted on 15 October 2016 and entered into force on 1 January 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kigali Amendment?
o: India begins its HFC phase-down from 2028
India must achieve an 85% cut by 2047
x: India freezes HFCs by 2028 but begins its phase-down only from 2032.

s: Which organisation launched the Green Diwali campaign under Mission LiFE, running till 8 November 2026?
x: WWF-India runs the Green Diwali campaign under Mission LiFE till 8 November 2026.

s: After three new Rhysida centipede species were found in the Western Ghats in October 2026, India's Rhysida species number how many?
x: With the three new species, India now has 23 Rhysida centipede species.

s: Along with Malabar Christian College, which institution discovered three new Rhysida centipede species in the Western Ghats?
x: The discovery was made by the ZSI with Malabar Christian College, not the Botanical Survey of India.

s: AATAL, launched on 25 October 2026 by Dr. Jitendra Singh, is the world's first integrated analysis centre for what?
o: Water pollution in the Yamuna basin
Air pollution in the Kolkata region
x: AATAL is the world's first integrated air pollution analysis centre for Delhi-NCR.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNEP's Emissions Gap Report of October 2026?
o: It is the 17th edition of the report
It puts global emissions at 58.4 Gt CO2e in 2025
It says an 18% cut is needed by 2030
It says a 45% cut is needed by 2030
x: The report needs cuts of 18% by 2030; 45% is the cut needed by 2035.

s: The name of Cyclone Arnab (October 2026, Bay of Bengal), meaning 'ocean/sea', was given by which country?
x: Arnab is a name given by Bangladesh and means 'ocean/sea'.

s: The cyclone name 'Murasu', proposed by India in November 2026, is a word of which language and means what?
x: 'Murasu' is a Tamil name proposed by India and means war drum.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Arnab means 'ocean/sea', not mountain. Arnab was named by Bangladesh and Murasu (war drum) by India.

s: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck the Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands on 26 October 2026. These islands belong to which country?
x: The Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands belong to Japan.

s: What is the capacity of the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, against which protests took place in October 2026?
x: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is an 11,200 MW project; protests took place at Pasighat.

s: Where did protests against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project take place in October 2026?
x: Clashes against the 11,200 MW project took place at Pasighat, not Tezu.

s: According to IUCN in October 2026, what share of shallow-water coral reef ecosystems is at risk of collapse by 2075?
x: IUCN said 96% of shallow-water coral reef ecosystems are at risk of collapse by 2075.

s: A UNFCCC report of 29 October 2026 says full implementation of NDCs would cut emissions by only how much by 2035, compared with 2019?
x: The UNFCCC report says full NDCs would cut emissions only 9% by 2035 compared with 2019.

s: Osbeckia assamensis, a new plant reported in October 2026, was found in which protected area?
x: Osbeckia assamensis was found in Manas National Park and reported in Phytotaxa.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the new plant species reported in October 2026?
o: Osbeckia assamensis belongs to the family Melastomataceae.
Osbeckia assamensis was reported in the journal Phytotaxa.
Ophiorrhiza shidiensis was found in Changlang, Arunachal Pradesh.
Ophiorrhiza pemae belongs to the family Melastomataceae.
x: Ophiorrhiza pemae belongs to the family Rubiaceae, not Melastomataceae.

s: In October 2026, Maharashtra approved which of the following as wildlife sanctuaries?
x: Maharashtra approved Kolamarka and an expanded Tansa among its new wildlife sanctuaries.

s: Ophiorrhiza shidiensis and Ophiorrhiza pemae were discovered in October 2026 in which district of Arunachal Pradesh?
x: Both species were found in Changlang by BSI and MCC and reported in the journal Taiwania.

s: Dicharax tilariensis, reported in November 2026 from Tilari in Kolhapur, is a new species of what?
x: Dicharax tilariensis is a microscopic land snail found at Tilari, Kolhapur.

s: According to India's report at FAO COFO 28 (2026), what is India's forest and tree cover?
x: At COFO 28, India's forest and tree cover was put at 82.74 million ha, or 25.17%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the FAO COFO 28 meeting of 2026?
o: It was held in Rome from 28 September to 2 October 2026
India reported its forest and tree cover as 25.17%
The State of the World's Forests 2026 puts degraded land at 1.65 billion ha
It was held along with the 10th World Forest Week
x: The State of the World's Forests 2026 puts degraded land at 1.56 billion ha, not 1.65 billion ha.

s: Which agency monitored the Mayon eruption of 1 November 2026?
x: The Mayon eruption was monitored by PHIVOLCS, not PAGASA.

s: UNEP's 17th Emissions Gap Report (2026) says emissions must be cut by how much by 2040?
x: The report needs cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about COP17 of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)?
o: It was held in Yerevan, Armenia.
It was held from 19 to 31 October 2026.
Its theme was "Taking Action for Nature".
CBD COP18 will be held in Quito, Ecuador, in 2030.
x: CBD COP18 will be held in Quito, Ecuador, in 2028, not 2030.

s: Where is Sukhna Wetland, designated a Ramsar site in October 2026, located?
x: Sukhna Wetland is in Chandigarh; Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh) was added the same day.

s: By which year are 96% of shallow-water coral reef ecosystems at risk of collapse, according to IUCN's warning of October 2026?
x: IUCN's warning is about collapse by 2075, not 2050.
